A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Transformer/LCG study. The main text, equations, figures, references, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original training results, prediction accuracies, scaling experiments, attention interventions, and seed analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional prime-modulus experiments, composite-modulus PCA analyses, and revised attention-masking results.

M1.justification: The GPT-style prediction models, training objective, base-b tokenization, and modified abacus embeddings are retained. Revised attention masking concerns diagnostic experiments; it does not establish a change to the underlying prediction method.

E1.justification: New Appendix C explicitly evaluates prime moduli: 2039 in fixed-modulus training and 1801/2039 in unseen-modulus testing. This adds a focused structural test scenario lacking the composite moduli's digit-wise periodic simplifications, while retaining the same LCG prediction tasks.

E2.justification: No predictive baseline method is added or removed. Comparisons remain among Transformer configurations, interventions, and LCG settings; the new prime-versus-composite experiments extend input coverage rather than comparator membership.

E3.justification: Appendix H.4 in v1 reports 4 million sequences and 2 million training steps; v2 Appendix I.4 reports 16 million sequences and 400,000 steps, retaining batch size 128. v2 also adds controlled prime-modulus experiments and changes the masking description from highest-scoring keys to specified power-of-two offsets. These are substantive reported protocol revisions, without establishing reruns. The actual dataset size remains ambiguous because v2 also retains the total of 4,194,304 sequences.

E4.justification: The revised masking experiment directly reassesses which attention connections suffice for higher-bit prediction (v1 Figure 19 versus v2 Figure 6). New Appendix C tests dependence on prime versus composite moduli, and Figures 26–27 add embedding PCA for composite moduli 7776 and 1800. These materially extend and revise the mechanism and applicability analyses.

E5.justification: The five-run summaries, median and min-max reporting, and separate model/data seed analyses are retained in Appendix H.3 versus I.3. No new repeated-run, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: v1 Figure 19(c) and Section 4.2 report poor higher-bit prediction when retaining two highest-scoring keys; v2 Figure 6(b) reports good higher-bit prediction with two specified positions retained. New Figures 18–19 report fixed-modulus failure at 2039 but strong unseen-modulus performance on prime cases; Figures 26–27 add composite embedding findings. These are revised or additional results, not demonstrated same-setting improvements to the prediction model.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects mathematical indexing: Equation (2) restores the missing 2^1 term, Equation (4) changes the residual modulus exponent from w_q to w_j, and the binary-period discussion changes alpha_w to alpha_(w-1). The appendix derivations themselves are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: fixed-modulus prediction up to 2^32, unseen-modulus prediction up to 2^16, factorization/RNS-based mechanisms, a three-layer threshold for unseen moduli, and sublinear context scaling.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 changes the explanation from faint attention connections being crucial for higher bits to the second principal connection supporting good higher-bit prediction. Appendices B–C qualify fixed-modulus learnability for prime moduli and hypothesize that diverse-modulus training encourages more general mechanisms. The new Impact Statement also explicitly limits applicability to mainstream cryptographic systems.

D1.justification: Reported large-modulus UM training time changes from 85.47 to 22.62 hours on the same single H100, with corresponding rounded updates in Appendix A.4. New experiment captions provide configurations and budgets, and masking is explicitly described as zeroing attention weights. Existing code access and general implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Doshi et al.'s Grokking modular polynomials and McCracken et al.'s work on an abstract algorithm for modular addition. These extend the modular-arithmetic and mechanism context without substantially changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites and condenses the mechanistic exposition, particularly Section 4.3, alongside revisions to the abstract and scaling discussion. It adds numbered Sections 5.1–5.2, a Prime Moduli appendix, and an Impact Statement. The extent of prose revision exceeds localized copyediting despite retaining the overall scientific narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds prime-modulus Figures 18–19 and composite-PCA Figures 26–27. The three-panel appendix masking display becomes a two-panel main-text Figure 6 with a longer displayed token-position range. Several retained figures move or receive shorter captions, while most plots and the overall visual format remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new prime-modulus tests expose an applicability boundary absent from v1, while additional composite PCA and more explicit masking experiments strengthen the mechanistic discussion. These provide a limited overall quality gain. The conflicting 4,194,304 and 16 million sequence counts in v2 Appendix I.4 weaken reproducibility, and the revised budgets do not establish an efficiency improvement.
